project.objective: Who did Amelia Frances Gioiello marry, and what evidence is found for their marriage?

questions.question: Whom did Amelia Frances Gioiello, daughter of Joseph Gioiello and Lena Manro, marry, and what records document that marriage?
questions.rationale: The research objective is to identify Amelia Frances Gioiello's husband and the evidence for their marriage. No sources currently support a marriage for Amelia in the tree. Marriage records, census records, and vital registrations from her likely adult years are the primary record types to search. This is the sole question needed to satisfy the objective.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All plan items completed or appropriately skipped. The original Trumbull County, Ohio marriage license and certificate (src_002, image ARK 3:1:3QSQ-G9WJ-M3P, license No. 43517) directly answers the question: Amelia Frances Gioiello married Stanley Datchuk on 20 August 1955 in Niles, Ohio. This original official document was certified by both parties under sworn oath before Probate Judge Sydney W. Jones, and the marriage was certified by officiating priest Father Nicholas Arioli C.P.P.S.; the license was granted 18 Aug 1955 and filed/recorded 22 Aug 1955. The FamilySearch index (src_001) is the derivative form of the same record, confirming identical facts. Newspaper search returned no relevant results. Census searches were negative for 1900/1910 and inapplicable for 1920/1930 (subject born ~1935). Ancestry skipped as it accesses the same county register data. Independent verification from a second repository type was not found, but the overturn risk is negligible: the original civil record is court-filed with multiple independent informants (both parties, the judge, the officiant).

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: YES — the question is directly answered. Amelia Frances Gioiello married Stanley Datchuk on 20 August 1955 in Niles, Trumbull County, Ohio. Certified in the original county marriage certificate by Father Nicholas Arioli C.P.P.S. and filed with the Probate Court.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: YES — FamilySearch Ohio County Marriages (positive, pli_004); FamilySearch GenealogyBank Newspapers (negative, pli_005); FamilySearch 1900/1910 US Census (negative, pli_001/002); 1920/1930 census inapplicable (subject born ~Nov 1935, not yet in existence). Ancestry fallback skipped as it accesses the same county register data (not an independent source). Original county register image accessed via image-reader (log_008).
stop_criteria.original_substitution: YES — src_001 (FamilySearch derivative index of Ohio County Marriages, collection 1614804) was supplemented by src_002, the original county marriage license and certificate image at ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G9WJ-M3P. The original is the controlling source; it confirms all indexed facts and adds birthplace (Niles, Ohio), residence addresses, occupations, officiant identity, and parental consent signatures.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: PARTIAL — src_001 (derivative) and src_002 (original) represent the same underlying county marriage register: one source in two forms, not two independent sources. No second independent repository produced a record. However, the original document itself was attested by multiple independent informants — both parties under sworn oath, Probate Judge Sydney W. Jones (license), and Father Nicholas Arioli (ceremony certificate) — giving it the weight of multiple certifications. The newspaper search was genuinely negative. Overturn risk is assessed as negligible.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: YES — src_002 is an original record containing primary information: both parties stated their own ages, birthplaces, residences, occupations, and parents' names under sworn oath before a judge. The officiant's certificate is direct primary evidence of the marriage event.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Minor conflicts noted but do not affect the marriage question: (1) Amelia's birth year: indexed 1936 vs. original image ~1935 — original controls; (2) Stanley's birth year: indexed 1933 vs. original ~1932 — original controls; (3) Stanley's mother's maiden name: derivative 'Mynarchyk' vs. original 'Synarehyk' — likely handwriting variant, original controls. None of these conflicts bear on who Amelia married or when.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: LOW. The original Trumbull County Probate Court marriage license and certificate (No. 43517) is an official civil document with sworn oaths, a judicial order, an officiant's certification, and court filing. No unsearched record type — church register, later census, death records — is plausibly likely to name a different groom or contradict the 20 August 1955 date and Niles, Ohio location. The conclusion is defensible.

items.rationale: The 1900 US Census lists all household members by name with exact birth month/year and birthplace. Searching for Amelia Gioiello (with variants) will establish her approximate birth year, birthplace, and parents' state of residence — the foundational facts needed to scope all subsequent marriage searches to the correct state and time period. Parents Joseph Gioiello and Lena Manro have no dates or places in the tree; this census will also confirm their presence and origins.

The 1910 US Census may show Amelia in her parents' household as a young woman, or in her own married household. It also records years of marriage ('YrsMar') for married persons, which would pinpoint when the marriage occurred if she is already wed. Searching alongside the 1900 result will track her across the decade.

The 1920 US Census may show Amelia in her own married household under her husband's surname. Cross-referencing with the 1910 result (same person, different name after marriage) will identify the husband and household location. If not yet found married, this census narrows the marriage window further.

FamilySearch 'United States, Marriages, 1733-1990' (collection 1675543) is a national marriage index aggregating state-level marriage records. Searching for Amelia Gioiello (and spelling variants: Giojello, Gioello, Giojello) may return a direct marriage record naming her husband, the marriage date, and county. This is the most direct source for the question; it should be searched in parallel with census work.

FamilySearch 'United States, GenealogyBank Historic Newspaper Marriages, 1815-2011' (collection 2603807) contains digitized newspaper marriage announcements. An announcement for Amelia Gioiello would name the groom, date, and sometimes officiant or witnesses, providing corroborating evidence for any marriage record found in step 4. Distinctive Italian surname makes false-positive matches unlikely.

Fallback if 1920 census does not locate Amelia as married. The 1930 US Census would show her in her married household with children's ages indicating approximate marriage date. Also useful as a cross-check if 1920 census finds her married but husband's name is ambiguous.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Marriage of Amelia Frances Gioiello to Stanley Datchuk

**Question:** Whom did Amelia Frances Gioiello marry, and what records document that marriage?

**Conclusion (Probable):** The preponderance of evidence strongly indicates that Amelia Frances Gioiello, daughter of Joseph Gioiello and Lena Mauro of Niles, Trumbull County, Ohio, married Stanley Datchuk, son of George Datchuk and Sarah Synarehyk, on 20 August 1955 in Niles, Trumbull County, Ohio.

### Primary Evidence

The controlling source is the original Trumbull County, Ohio Marriage License No. 43517.[^1] Both Amelia Frances Gioiello and Stanley Datchuk appeared before Probate Judge Sydney W. Jones and swore to their application on 13 August 1955. Amelia, then 19 years old (birthday 16 November, born approximately 1935), gave her residence as 815 Henry Street, Niles, Ohio, and her occupation as Clerk; her father Joseph Gioiello and mother Lena Gioiello (née Mauro) signed as parental consent witnesses. Stanley, then 22 years old (birthday 14 September, born approximately 1932), gave his residence as 530 Baldwin, Niles, Ohio, and his occupation as Carpenter; he named his father as George Datchuk and his mother's maiden name as Sarah Synarehyk. ### Discrepancies Assessed

Three minor discrepancies between the original image and the derivative index were noted; none affects the identity of the parties or the fact of the marriage:

1. **Bride's birth year.** The derivative index gives 1936; the original application states the bride was 19 years of age as of 16 November 1954, implying birth approximately November 1935. The original sworn testimony controls over the derivative index.
2. **Groom's birth year.** The derivative index gives 1933; the original application states the groom was 22 years of age as of 14 September 1954, implying birth approximately September 1932. The original sworn testimony controls.
3. **Groom's mother's maiden name.** The derivative index renders the surname as "Mynarchyk"; the original image reads "Synarehyk." Both appear to be alternative handwriting interpretations of the same Eastern European (likely Ukrainian) surname. The original image reading controls; a corroborating record would confirm the correct spelling.

### Confidence Tier

This conclusion is assessed at the **probable** tier. The original Trumbull County marriage license and certificate is a single high-quality original source with primary information, attested by multiple parties; no second genuinely independent source was located. A "proved" conclusion would require at least two independent original sources. The Catholic parish marriage register of Father Arioli's church in Niles, Ohio (a Congregation of the Precious Blood parish) would constitute a genuinely independent source and could advance this conclusion to "proved" if located and examined. Absent such a second independent source, the available evidence strongly supports the conclusion but does not yet meet the full GPS proof standard.
